## 15.1 The Werner resource read in three correlators

$\rho_V=V|\Phi^+\rangle\langle\Phi^+|+(1-V)\tfrac{I}{4}$ has $qg_{XX}=V$, $qg_{YY}=-V$, $qg_{ZZ}=V$ (Ch. 7: single-basis correlators each, 0 ancillas). Singlet fraction and mean teleportation fidelity (Horodecki):
$$F_s=\tfrac14\big(1+qg_{XX}-qg_{YY}+qg_{ZZ}\big),\qquad \bar F=\frac{2F_s+1}{3},\qquad \bar F_{\text{Werner}}=\frac{1+V}{2}.$$
Classical threshold $\bar F=2/3\iff F_s=1/2\iff V=1/3$: **the Bell pair is useful if and only if $qg_{ZZ}>333$ m-qg** under the Werner model (`exact`). For a general resource all 3 bases are needed; the single-basis reading is an upper bound (§15.4). The Werner resource is read as three single-basis correlators; the classical threshold is $qg_{ZZ}=333$ m-qg under the Werner model, and an upper bound otherwise.

The threshold $qg_{ZZ}=1/3$ ($333$ m-qg) marks the limit for better-than-classical teleportation and, in the Werner model, for entanglement; it does not mark Bell violation: the Werner family violates CHSH only for $V>1/\sqrt2$. The singlet fraction $F_s=(1+qg_{XX}-qg_{YY}+qg_{ZZ})/4$ refers to $|\Psi^-\rangle$; with $\rho_V$ mixed with $|\Phi^+\rangle$ the correlators are $(+V,-V,+V)$. The Bell convention changes the sign of $qg_{YY}$, not $\bar F$.

**Sources for this section.** R. Werner, *Phys. Rev. A* 40, 4277 (1989), DOI `10.1103/PhysRevA.40.4277`, <https://journals.aps.org/pra/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevA.40.4277>; M. Horodecki, P. Horodecki and R. Horodecki, *Phys. Rev. A* 60, 1888 (1999), DOI `10.1103/PhysRevA.60.1888`, <https://arxiv.org/html/quant-ph/9807091v2>.

## 15.2 The teleportation channel in m-qg: m'=V m

Full teleportation (Bell measurement on input⊗A, Pauli correction on B) with resource $\rho_V$ is the depolarizing channel $\mathbf r\mapsto V\mathbf r$; in readout: $m\text{-qg}'=V\cdot m\text{-qg}$ for any axis, verified to $10^{-13}$ on random inputs. Example: $+600$ m-qg $\to+420$ ($V=0.7$) $\to+200$ ($V=1/3$). The dissipative deficit of the teleported state (Ch. 5) is $qg_\tau=\sqrt{1-V^2r^2}$. The average fidelity over the 2-design of 6 Pauli eigenstates reproduces $(1+V)/2$ to $10^{-13}$ (`exact`).

$m\text{-qg}'=V\,m\text{-qg}$ is the contraction of the depolarizing channel induced by imperfect teleportation, verified on 9 random inputs to $10^{-13}$; it does not imply physical attenuation or loss of the photon, but the average over the mixed resource.

**Sources for this section.** C. H. Bennett et al., *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 70, 1895 (1993), DOI `10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.1895`, <https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.1895>.

## 15.3 Shot budget and configurations

From $qg_{ZZ}$: $\sigma_{\bar F}=\tfrac12\sqrt{(1-V^2)/N}$ ⇒ $N=(1-V^2)/(4\sigma_{\bar F}^2)$: $475$ shots ($V=0.9$) or $1\,600$ ($V=0.6$) for $\sigma_{\bar F}=0.01$ in **one** configuration. Process tomography of the channel: 4 inputs $\times$ 3 bases $=12$ configurations, $\ge12N$ shots for the same precision per cell (`exact`, count).

The budget $N=(1-V^2)/(4\sigma_{\bar F}^2)$ assumes independent shots, a $qg_{ZZ}$ estimator without readout error, no dark counts and a known Werner form; it gives $475$ and $1\,600$ shots for $V=0.9$ and $0.6$. The comparison with $12N$ is at equal $\sigma$ per tomography cell, not at equal global information: a single basis does not reconstruct the full process.

## 15.4 `mixed` finding: the single-basis reading overestimates non-Werner resources

A resource with pure dephasing ($qg_{ZZ}=1$, $qg_{XX}=0.8$): real $\bar F$ (3 bases) $=0.9333$; $\bar F$ assuming Werner from $qg_{ZZ}$ $=1.0000$ (bias $+0.067$). Rule: **certify with 3 bases; plan with 1**. A resource with $qg_{ZZ}>1/3$ but $qg_{XX}+qg_{ZZ}\le1$ is not certified as entangled (2-basis witness, Ch. 5).

The bound $\bar F_{1\text{ basis}}\ge\bar F_{3\text{ bases}}$ was verified on the non-Werner state built in `verify_cap15.py` §5. The operational rule `plan with 1, certify with 3` is conservative; the chapter does not present it as a general theorem for every two-qubit state.

**Sources for this section.** D. Bouwmeester et al., *Nature* 390, 575 (1997), DOI `10.1038/37539`, <https://www.nature.com/articles/37539>; D. Boschi et al., *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 80, 1121 (1998), DOI `10.1103/PhysRevLett.80.1121`, <https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.80.1121>.

## 15.6 JAX block (`qang/qtele.py`)

```python
@jax.jit
def resource_correlators(rho2):                 # (qg_XX, qg_YY, qg_ZZ)
    f = lambda P: jnp.real(jnp.trace(rho2 @ jnp.kron(P, P)))
    return f(X), f(Y), f(Z)

@jax.jit
def singlet_fraction_from_qg(qxx, qyy, qzz):    # (1 + qg_XX − qg_YY + qg_ZZ)/4
    return (1.0 + qxx - qyy + qzz) / 4.0

@jax.jit
def teleport_fidelity_from_singlet(Fs):         # (2F_s + 1)/3 ; threshold 2/3
    return (2.0 * Fs + 1.0) / 3.0

def teleport(rho_in, rho_res):                  # Bell measurement + Pauli correction, ρ_out 2×2
    rho = kron(rho_in, rho_res); corr = [I2, Z, X, X @ Z]; out = 0
    for k, b in enumerate(bell_basis()):
        M = kron(jnp.outer(b, jnp.conj(b)), I2)
        rb = jnp.einsum("iaib->ab", (M @ rho @ M).reshape(4, 2, 4, 2))
        out = out + corr[k] @ rb @ jnp.conj(corr[k]).T
    return out

def shots_for_fidelity(V, sigma_F):             # (1 − V²)/(4σ_F²)
    return (1.0 - V ** 2) / (4.0 * sigma_F ** 2)
```

### `tests/test_qtele.py`
```python
import pytest; jax = pytest.importorskip("jax")
import numpy as np, jax.numpy as jnp
from qang.qtele import werner, teleport, bloch, state_from_bloch, teleport_fidelity_werner_qzz, resource_correlators

def test_channel_contracts_bloch():
    r = jnp.array([0.3, -0.4, 0.5]); out = teleport(state_from_bloch(r), werner(0.7))
    assert np.allclose(np.asarray(bloch(out)), 0.7 * np.asarray(r), atol=1e-13)

def test_classical_threshold_333_mqg():
    assert abs(float(teleport_fidelity_werner_qzz(1 / 3)) - 2 / 3) < 1e-15

def test_werner_correlators():
    qxx, qyy, qzz = resource_correlators(werner(0.5))
    assert abs(float(qxx) - 0.5) < 1e-14 and abs(float(qyy) + 0.5) < 1e-14 and abs(float(qzz) - 0.5) < 1e-14
```

## 15.9 Experiment 12/13.1 — Teleported fidelity from three correlators and the dual-rail filter

**Identity note.** Former §13.1 in the historical index («teleportation fidelity as a linear reading of three qg correlators») was rewritten in Chs. 15–16; it is verified here as one experiment with its optical part.

**Hypothesis.** $\bar F=(3+qg_{XX}-qg_{YY}+qg_{ZZ})/6$ predicts fidelity without running the teleportation circuit; Werner $V=0.9$ gives $0.95$, while a non-Werner state with $(0.8,-0.8,1.0)$ gives $0.9333$ versus $1.0$ if one wrongly assumes a single basis. In a 50 km dual rail, $\eta=0.1$: unfiltered reads $+0.84$, filtered reads $-0.60$ at rate $0.10$.

**Method.** `tools/verify_exp12_13_1.py` uses `qang.qpon.fidelity_from_correlators`, `qang.qtele.teleport_fidelity_werner_qzz`/`shots_for_fidelity` and `qang.qdualrail` (`transmission`, `dual_rail_state`, `apply_loss`, `readout_unfiltered`, `readout_sector_filtered`, `shots_multiplier_two_photons`), without Qiskit.

```text
exact algebra: F=1 (Bell), F=2/3 at qg_ZZ=1/3; N(F=0.9, σ=0.01)=475
Werner V=0.9: F=0.950000; non-Werner: F=0.933333 vs 1 basis=1.000000
V=0.9000: F̂=0.949183 vs 0.950000 (±0.000890)
V=0.3333: F̂=0.667917 vs 0.666667 (±0.001925)
50 km dual rail: η=0.10, raw=+0.84, filtered=-0.60 (rate 0.10)
```

**Reading.** Three bases suffice to predict $\bar F$ and expose the Werner-assumption bias; the sector filter removes the loss bias at $\times1/\eta$ shots. `exact` in simulation; hardware `unverified`.
